questions.question_text: Define the concept of globalization in the modern economic context. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Globalization is the process of rapid integration or interconnection between countries through free trade, foreign investments, and the extensive exchange of technology and cultural ideas.

questions.question_text: Why is the manufacturing sector considered the backbone of economic development? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: The manufacturing sector transforms raw materials into valuable finished goods. It is considered the backbone of economic development because it provides jobs, reduces poverty, and boosts exports.

questions.question_text: What is the core principle of sustainable development? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Sustainable development refers to achieving economic growth that meets present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs, ensuring long-term environmental protection.

questions.question_text: Explain how unchecked industries cause severe water pollution. [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Industries often discharge untreated organic and inorganic chemical effluents directly into rivers and lakes. This toxic industrial waste severely contaminates the water, destroying fragile aquatic ecosystems.

questions.question_text: What is the role of Information Technology in the growth of modern industries? [20-30 words]
questions.answer: Information Technology facilitates global communication and rapid data transfer. It helps modern industries manage complex supply chains, automate production, and connect with international markets instantly.

questions.question_text: Imagine you visit a modern automobile manufacturing plant. Describe the assembly line and the advanced technology used there. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: The plant features a highly automated assembly line where robotic arms efficiently weld and assemble car parts with precision. Advanced sensors monitor quality in real-time, while skilled workers oversee the complex machinery, ensuring seamless, high-speed mass production of modern vehicles.

questions.question_text: Think about how globalization affects local cultures. Describe both a positive and a negative impact on daily life. [40-50 words]
questions.answer: Globalization introduces diverse international cuisines, global fashion, and advanced technologies, significantly enriching local lifestyles. However, it negatively impacts heritage by threatening traditional cultural practices, often leading to a gradual loss of unique regional identities as massive global brands dominate local markets.

questions.question_text: Analyze the environmental consequences of rapid industrialization and suggest two actionable measures a government can take to promote 'Happy and Healthy Living'. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Rapid industrialization severely degrades the natural environment through massive greenhouse gas emissions, deforestation, and toxic waste dumping in rivers. To ensure healthier living, the government must strictly enforce anti-pollution laws, mandate the installation of waste treatment plants in all factories, and heavily subsidize renewable energy sources to promote sustainable growth.

questions.question_text: Explain how the integration of global markets connects 'Different Lands and Different Lives', using the example of a multinational corporation setting up production in a developing country. [50-60 words]
questions.answer: Global market integration closely links distant nations by sharing resources and labor. When an MNC sets up a factory in a developing country, it brings advanced technology and creates local employment opportunities. However, it also intertwines their economies, meaning a financial crisis in one land directly affects lives everywhere.
